findings.title: ICU MessageFormat choice syntax injected into i18next (double-brace) translation file
findings.body: The value for 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' was changed from 'Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).' to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.'. Every other key in this file (and the whole account-ui/admin-ui message bundle) uses i18next's double-curly-brace interpolation syntax ({{0}}) and i18next pluralization suffixes (e.g. resourceSharedWith_one/_zero/_other), not Java's single-brace MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat. react-i18next does not interpret '{0,choice,...}' syntax, so the UI will render the literal unprocessed string instead of a correctly pluralized sentence. This appears to be the Java-theme fix (which is appropriate for FreeMarker/MessageFormat-based themes) mistakenly applied to the JS UI translation bundle as well.

findings.title: Same ICU choice-format regression applied to Admin UI i18next messages
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from the i18next double-brace form 'Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).' to a Java ChoiceFormat string 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.'. This file feeds the React admin console (i18next), which uses {{var}} interpolation and _one/_other plural key suffixes, not inline ChoiceFormat syntax. The new string will be displayed verbatim to admins instead of being properly interpolated/pluralized, breaking this specific validation error message in the Admin Console UI.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The fix for the illegal-HTML content in 'totpStep1' replaced the Lithuanian sentence with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian-locale users will now see Italian text for this instruction. The same incorrect replacement text appears in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties for 'loginTotpStep1'.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian, when removing the disallowed anchor tags. This is a content/locale regression introduced while fixing the HTML sanitization issue; the replacement text should be a correct Lithuanian translation.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file populated with Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: totpStep1 was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式) inappropriate for a zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) locale file. Users of the Simplified Chinese locale will see Traditional Chinese characters mixed into otherwise Simplified Chinese text.

findings.title: Missing/unreadable English reference file crashes the whole build instead of reporting a validation error
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() computes the path of the English reference file via a brittle string-replace heuristic (replacing "resources-community" with "resources" and the locale suffix with "_en.properties"), then wraps any IOException from reading it in an unchecked RuntimeException (lines 76-80). Because verify() only catches IOException, this RuntimeException propagates uncaught out of verify(), aborting the whole Maven build with a raw stack trace instead of producing a MojoExecutionException or an entry in the returned messages list. Since theme-verifier-maven-plugin is packaged as a general-purpose plugin, any theme/module whose directory layout doesn't match this exact convention (or that lacks an '_en' counterpart) will crash the build rather than fail gracefully with an actionable message.

findings.title: No tests cover the hardcoded per-key normalization exceptions
findings.body: normalizeValue() hardcodes special handling for specific keys ('templateHelp', 'optimizeLookupHelp', and keys starting with 'linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit' or equal to 'error-invalid-multivalued-size') to avoid false-positive HTML/illegal-tag detections caused by legitimate '<NAME>'/'<Extensions>'/ChoiceFormat syntax. None of the added tests exercise these branches, so regressions in this fragile, key-name-based allowlist (e.g. a new key using '{0,choice,...}' syntax not added to the list) would silently be flagged as illegal HTML with no test coverage to catch it.

findings.title: HTML sanitizer policies rebuilt for every file instance
findings.body: POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are non-static instance fields rebuilt via HtmlPolicyBuilder().toFactory() every time a VerifyMessageProperties object is constructed (i.e., once per properties file being verified). Since these policies are stateless and identical across all files, they should be static final fields shared across instances, avoiding unnecessary object construction for every theme message file scanned.

findings.title: ANCHOR_PATTERN overly broad, matches tags other than anchors
findings.body: ANCHOR_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>") matches any tag whose name starts with the letter 'a' (e.g. '<address>', '<abbr>'), not just '<a>' anchor tags, because '[^>]*' allows any following characters. This can cause santizeAnchors() to mislabel and process non-anchor tags as if they were anchors, producing a misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' message for tags that are not actually anchors.
